title: Mandatory electronic conveyancing (Western Australia)
summary: Landgate required eligible transfers to be lodged electronically from 1 December 2018.

instruments.title: Registrar of Titles' requirements under the Electronic Conveyancing Act 2014 (WA)

commenced.what: Electronic lodgment required for eligible transfers

direction_rationale: Mandatory electronic lodgment cuts settlement costs and time for conveyancers and lenders, but in practice it entrenched one electronic lodgment network (PEXA), because interoperability between networks never went live.
comparison: Staggered mandates 2018-2023; the ACT, Tasmania and the NT have no mandate (never treated)
confounders: housing market swings and interest rate changes

verified.notes: Date from Landgate customer information bulletin 315.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Requires property transfers and mortgages to be lodged electronically. Settlement is faster and cheaper, but with no working interoperability between networks the mandate entrenched a single lodgement network.

marks.reason: Electronic lodgement and settlement cut paperwork, settlement time and errors.
Moves conveyancing onto a digital platform.
Without interoperability, mandatory electronic lodgement entrenched one network (PEXA) as a near-monopoly supplier.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on business entry in legal services (grade Weak).
